automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Only public records with a visible, precise publication or update timestamp strictly inside this two-day window are retained.

source_method: Public-web discovery followed by direct public CVE Program API and first-party vendor/advisory verification; no local or private content was sent externally.
searched_topics: agent and tool security including MCP and delegated authority
identity authentication authorization credentials and least privilege
AI supply chains and deployment runtimes
AI security governance and public incidents

qualifying_findings.summary: llama.cpp before b10261 has a heap out-of-bounds write in the plamo2 tokenizer build path; a crafted GGUF model can corrupt memory during model loading, causing crashes or potential code execution.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: llama.cpp b5899 before b10261; crafted GGUF model/tokenizer input.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model artifacts are executable-risk supply-chain inputs, so loading must be treated as a hostile-data boundary.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: llama.cpp background belongs in ai-wiki; retain the model-artifact loading security implication locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Verify the upstream fixed build and any distributor backports before synthesis.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVIDIA PSIRT security bulletin corroborated by CVE Program public record
qualifying_findings.summary: NVIDIA disclosed a critical missing-authentication issue (CVSS 10.0) in NeMo Agent Toolkit 1.0-1.8.0 that can lead to code execution, privilege escalation, data tampering, denial of service, and disclosure; the same bulletin also fixes SQL injection in 1.4-1.6.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: NeMo Agent Toolkit: CVE-2026-65145 affects 1.0-1.8.0 and is fixed in 1.9.0; CVE-2026-65151 affects 1.4-1.6 and is fixed in 1.7.0.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent runtimes need authentication on critical functions and must patch their deployed toolkit version, not only application code.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: NVIDIA and NeMo product context are upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain local identity and agent-runtime control implications.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: At ingest, determine the exposed service endpoints and whether dependent deployments require an urgent version inventory.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Program record and public advisory
qualifying_findings.summary: The official MCP Python SDK followed cross-origin redirects in HTTP, SSE, OAuth, and related client paths, forwarding caller-supplied credential headers and sometimes request bodies to a redirected origin.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: 1.8.0 through before 1.30.0 and 2.0.0 through before 2.2.0; fixed in 1.30.0 and 2.2.0.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP client trust must bind credentials and request payloads to the configured origin; redirect handling is an authorization boundary.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MCP catalog context is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the security-specific credential and redirect boundary locally.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Inventory SDK versions and review custom-header use on MCP HTTP endpoints.

qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Primary security-research disclosure corroborated by CVE Program record
qualifying_findings.summary: Pillar disclosed that a malicious nested model_type value in a model config can reach an exec()-built import in Unsloth's model-loading compiler, executing arbitrary Python even when trust_remote_code is false.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Unsloth Zoo 2025.9.9 before 2026.8.14 as used by Unsloth 2025.9.9 through 2026.8.19; fixed dependency floor in Unsloth 2026.8.20.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model configuration is an untrusted supply-chain input; a remote-code opt-out does not protect a loader that turns metadata into Python source.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Unsloth and Hugging Face ecosystem context are upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain local model-loader supply-chain implications.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Check notebooks, training workers, and images for affected Unsloth Zoo and Unsloth versions.

qualifying_findings.summary: DroidMind through 0.4.0 lets MCP clients bypass a shell-command allowlist with $() or backticks, including from prompt-injected agent input.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: DroidMind through 0.4.0; Device.run_shell and unvalidated Device.list_directory inputs.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Command allowlists do not safely mediate agent-controlled shell strings.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Product context is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain local agent-to-device command-boundary implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: No fixed version is identified in the CVE record; isolate or disable affected server tooling pending a patch.

qualifying_findings.summary: ATXP Gemini CLI extension through 1.0.0 accepts unsanitized MCP email and SMS parameters in runAtxp(), enabling shell injection through prompt-planted content.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ATXP Gemini CLI extension through 1.0.0; message_id, subject, and query parameters.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Untrusted message content must not become tool command syntax through agent delegation.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Gemini product context is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain local delegated-tool injection implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: No fixed version is identified in the CVE record; remove or sandbox the extension until patched.

qualifying_findings.summary: Codefriar sf-mcp through 1.3.2 passes crafted Salesforce CLI flag values through an incomplete escape helper to execSync, allowing shell command execution as the MCP-server user.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: sf-mcp through 1.3.2; Salesforce CLI tool-flag values.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Escaping helpers are not a substitute for argument-vector execution at an agent tool boundary.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Tool catalog context is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain local command-execution control implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: No fixed version is identified in the CVE record; use array-based process invocation after a maintainer fix.

qualifying_findings.summary: esp-mcp through commit 28afddf sends agent-controlled tool parameters to asyncio.create_subprocess_shell, allowing prompt-injection-reachable shell execution.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: esp-mcp through commit 28afddf9ff41ada117bb45fd49b526d3bf89749e; target, port, project_path, and project_name.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Tool arguments must remain data through process execution, especially when agents can be induced to call them.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Tool catalog context is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain local agent-shell boundary implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Pin away from the affected commit or disable the server; no fixed release is identified.

qualifying_findings.summary: mcp-ffmpeg through 1.0.5 builds child_process.exec strings from videoPath and outputDir, permitting shell injection from crafted names.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mcp-ffmpeg through 1.0.5; resize-video, extract-audio, and get-video-info tool inputs.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A file path drawn from agent context can be attacker-controlled input to a privileged media-processing tool.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Tool catalog context is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain local file-to-command boundary implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: No fixed version is identified in the CVE record; sandbox server execution and avoid shell-string construction.

qualifying_findings.summary: Kali-GPT through commit a608c74 runs unsanitized scanner parameters with subprocess.run(shell=True), allowing MCP clients or prompt-injected agents to execute commands as the server user.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Kali-GPT through commit a608c74e99910232dd208fee99de860458672b82; scanner target, ports, domain, wordlist, and URL fields.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Security-scanning agents amplify the harm of command injection because their tools often run with broad network and host privileges.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Tool catalog context is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain local security-tool delegated-authority implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: No fixed release is identified; restrict network reach and disable shell-string execution.

qualifying_findings.summary: Vorota-ai nmap-mcp lets callers bypass its script-category allowlist and run intrusive, brute-force, exploit, or denial-of-service Nmap scripts.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: nmap-mcp through commit 3636afa6ad4e159c7ad07ca35ede644f37db9c5e; scan_vulnerabilities category control.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent authorization policies must bind a requested action to an independently enforced capability, not a bypassable classification string.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Tool catalog context is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain local delegated scanning-authorization implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: No fixed release is identified; disable intrusive categories at the execution layer.

qualifying_findings.summary: hagent through commit 761eec6 interpolates args from MCP tool calls into Arduino CLI and idf.py shell commands, allowing command execution.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: hagent through commit 761eec627a1e6fb128a2a8ce9245aa595cc2f7af; hagent_arduino and hagent_esp32 args.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent control over embedded-device tooling needs process isolation and argument-level validation because the server identity is the execution authority.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Tool catalog context is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain local agent-to-device execution implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: No fixed release is identified; disable or isolate the affected server until a non-shell invocation patch is available.

exclusions.candidate: AI security/news aggregators and event pages
exclusions.reason: Used for discovery only when a primary CVE, vendor bulletin, or primary research disclosure could not be verified; ordinary announcements and date-only pages were not retained.

confidence_notes: All retained timing comes from precise CVE Program timestamps except the Unsloth research-disclosure date, which is visibly dated October 27 on the primary Pillar Security page; its CVE timestamp is recorded separately and is older.
The eight newly retained MCP server records are separate affected tools and each has a direct CVE Program record; fixed releases are absent where the record does not identify one.
No docs/wiki or raw/processed content was changed by this collection run.

Recheck maintainer fixes for all MCP tools whose CVE record lacks a fixed version or release.
